about: Golden vectors for canonicalization and hashing of Ductus evidence v2 (DAN-127). All data is invented.
The file is ASCII: every non-ASCII character is written as a \u escape. Read it with a JSON parser from the file bytes, not through a bundler import, which may rewrite keys such as __proto__.

The expected values were derived outside the repository (RFC texts, hand-written canonical strings, an independent implementation). Never regenerate them from the code under test: a change that alters any value is a change of the evidence contract.

definitions.canonicalBytes: UTF-8 encoding of the RFC 8785 (JCS) serialization of a JSON value. No Unicode normalization. A lone surrogate or a non-finite number has no canonical form.
definitions.documentHash: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the canonical document JSON.
definitions.segmentHash: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of an evidence segment v2. The server hashes the bytes it received and accepts them only when they are the canonical bytes of a valid segment.
definitions.chain: predecessorSegmentHash is the segmentHash of the segment accepted before it, null for the first. The head is the last segmentHash together with the number of segments.
definitions.segmentTime: observedStartedAt and observedEndedAt are whole minutes in UTC, written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:00.000Z. An event has no time; events are ordered by sequence.
definitions.eventSource: One of editor, paste, cut, drop, composition, system-replacement, keyless-input and unattributed; no other value and no default. editor is written only for a change positively attributed to typing in the editor. composition is written only when the capture layer has positive proof that the character was composed with physical keys; in every other case, also when there is no proof or the proof is ambiguous, keyless-input is written. keyless-input is text entered without key events (dictation, an on-screen keyboard, an input method with no such proof). unattributed is every change with no positive attribution, and a paste or a drop whose event cannot be relied on. The server cannot check these rules; the capture layer keeps them.
definitions.receiptDigest: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v1 (payloadDigestSha256).
definitions.receiptSignatureV1: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v1; raw 64-byte signature, base64url without padding. Decision D-92 replaces this for receipt v2.
definitions.receiptDigestV2: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v2 (payloadDigestSha256). D below is its 32 raw bytes.
definitions.receiptSignatureV2: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over the 59 bytes UTF-8(ductus-evidence-receipt-v2) || 0x0a || D (decision D-92); raw 64-byte signature, base64url without padding. Never over the canonical bytes of the payload and never over D alone.
definitions.evidenceDomainId: The identifier of an evidence domain (one institution in one region) in the signed receipt v2: a canonical lowercase version 4 UUID of 36 characters. Random, opaque and immutable; never derived from the id or the name of an institution, from a region or from a time.

chain.note: Two chained segments from the empty document to a signed receipt for each. Steps use an invented test format: insert-text at a UTF-16 offset of the text of one node. Receipts are signed with the Ed25519 test key published as TEST 1 in RFC 8032 section 7.1; only its public half is stored here. signingSeedSha256 is the SHA-256 of the 32 private bytes printed in the RFC, so that a test can show those bytes are in none of the vector files.

eventTime.note: Owner decision of 10 October 2026 (D-24, D-56): a segment carries no time per event and no time finer than a minute, and the server refuses a segment that does; it never rounds one. formerSegments are the two chain segments of the first revision of this file (DAN-127), byte for byte: canonical JCS that was valid then and must be refused now, because its events carry occurredAt and elapsedMs and its observed times carry seconds. formerSegmentHash is the hash that revision published for them. The edits with the classes event-time, time-precision, time-form and closed-shape under segmentPayloads.rejected, and time-in-capture-context, each break one rule on the current first segment.

sizeLimit.note: Set events[0].steps[0].text of segmentWithoutPadding to padding.unit repeated padding.count times. The unit is two UTF-8 bytes and one UTF-16 code unit, so the limit is seen to count bytes. The document hashes in the segment are those of the padded document. overLimit appends extraText to that text.

receiptV2.note: Receipt v2 (D-92, DAN-54). The signed payload carries revision, clientTransactionId and evidenceDomainId next to the fields of receipt v1. The signature is Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over signingInputHex: the 26 bytes of the text ductus-evidence-receipt-v2, one line feed (0x0a) and the 32 raw bytes of payloadDigestSha256, 59 bytes in all. accepted[0] is the contract vector of docs/BACKEND.md section 4.1, with the fields in the order of RFC 8785: clientTransactionId after acceptedAt, evidenceDomainId between eventCount and evidencePackageId, revision after receiptSchema. Signatures are made with the key chain.verificationKey. Both evidence domain ids are random version 4 UUIDs drawn for this file; they name no institution. revision and clientTransactionId mean the commit in which the segment of the receipt was accepted (owner decision of 11 October 2026, issue 87 comment 6105502093, point 5). A revision may have more than one receipt, and the sequence numbers of a segment say nothing about the revision: accepted[0] is the first receipt of its package and carries revision 7. A receipt v2 states three things: the bytes with segmentHash were received and stored, they continue the chain after predecessorSegmentHash, and the document whose hash is the finalDocumentHash of that segment was saved as revision. rejectedPayloads change accepted[0].payload: set replaces or adds fields, remove deletes them. The class acceptance-fields holds one change for each rule of the fields a receipt v2 shares with a receipt v1. rejectedSignatures are valid signatures of the same key over messageHex, which is not the signing input of accepted[0].
